assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to human NDE1 (Q9NXR1, canonical 335-aa isoform; verified by my global alignment). Every supporting annotation (IBA, ISS, IEA from InterPro IPR033494 and Ensembl orthology) traces back to two mouse annotations: an IMP for mouse Nde1 (PMID:15473967, Feng & Walsh 2004) and an IDA for mouse Ndel1 (PMID:11163259, Sasaki et al. 2000). Neither establishes direct microtubule binding. The Feng & Walsh abstract reports knockout phenotypes (spindle assembly, centrosome duplication, microcephaly), i.e. biological process, not binding. The Sasaki abstract reports LIS1/NUDEL/dynein-heavy-chain complex formation and colocalization; any microtubule association there is in the context of the dynein complex. When purified NudE was tested directly, it did not co-sediment with microtubules (McKenney et al. 2010, Fig. 2D). Mammalian Nde1/Ndel1 are described in reviews as reducing dynein's microtubule affinity, not as microtubule-binding proteins. NDE1 does localize to centrosomes, the spindle and microtubule plus ends at kinetochores, but this is CENPF/dynein-dependent and is not a binding activity. No evidence establishes the GO:0008017 activity for NDE1.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to rat Mcoln1/TRPML1 (A0A8I6G3L4, 579 aa). Dong et al. 2008 (Nature) showed that mouse TRPML1 is a Fe2+-permeable channel in late endosomes and lysosomes. They used radiolabelled iron uptake, cytosolic and intralysosomal iron measurements, and direct patch-clamp of endolysosomal membranes. ML4 point mutations impaired Fe2+ permeation. UniProt Q99J21 (mouse) records these mutagenesis results, and the human entry Q9GZU1 carries IDA for the same term. Transfer to rat is well supported. My global alignment gives 96.7% identity between the rat and mouse proteins. The pore-forming intramembrane segment (mouse 457-477, LSMVSECLFSLINGDDMFVTF) is 21/21 identical, and the TM5-pore-TM6 region (mouse 428-513) is 85/86 identical. Every mouse residue whose mutation abolished or reduced Fe2+ transport (T232, D362, R403, F408, V446, F465, and the V432 gating site) is conserved in rat. A channel that conducts Fe2+ across the lysosomal membrane meets the GO:0005381 definition of transferring iron ions from one side of a membrane to the other.

https://rest.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q9GZU1.txt - human TRPML1: Fe2+ transport reaction (RHEA:28486); GO:0005381 IDA

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to Rhizobium leguminosarum bv. viciae 3841 RgtB (Q1MJ97). The pentosyltransferase annotation is a TreeGrafter/PANTHER IEA. It comes from glycosyltransferase family GT83 (PTHR33908), whose reviewed members include ArnT, the undecaprenyl-phosphate-L-Ara4N (pentose) transferase. RgtB itself has been characterized experimentally, and it does not transfer a pentose. Expression cloning and in vitro membrane assays (Kanjilal-Kolar et al. 2006), identification of the donor as dodecaprenyl-phosphate-beta-D-galacturonic acid (Kanjilal-Kolar & Raetz 2006), and mutant core-structure analysis (Brown et al. 2012) all show that RgtB transfers galacturonic acid (GalA) to the outer Kdo of the LPS core, acting after RgtA. GalA is a six-carbon hexuronic acid, not a pentosyl group. UniProt accordingly annotates the protein with GO:0016758 hexosyltransferase activity (IMP). Membership of the GT83 family does not justify a pentosyl donor when the specific enzyme is shown to use a different sugar.

https://europepmc.org/abstract/MED/22110131 (PMC3256847) - Brown et al. 2012 JBC: rgtA, rgtB and rgtC use Dod-P-GalA to attach GalA to the LPS core; mutant core structures (abstract read)

assertions.limitations: The evidence does not merely fail to support the term; it identifies a hexuronic-acid (GalA) donor, which argues against the pentosyl claim. No study tested pentose donors with RgtB.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to mouse Irgm1 (Q60766, 409 aa). The only supporting annotation is an ISO from human IRGM (A1A4Y4). Human IRGM co-immunoprecipitates with ULK1, which supports protein kinase binding for the human protein (Chauhan et al. 2015, Fig. 1D-H and Fig. 3I). The same paper found that IRGM did not co-precipitate with AMPK (Fig. S1D). Transfer to mouse Irgm1 is not well supported. Human IRGM is a truncated, highly divergent primate gene. In my global alignment, its 181-aa canonical isoform covers only about 180 of the 409 mouse residues, with 56% identity over the aligned region (24.7% of the mouse sequence). UniProt A1A4Y4 states there is 'a huge difference in terms of sequence and regulation of expression compared to the mouse ortholog and hence, the function might be slightly different'. Chauhan et al. performed no experiments on mouse Irgm1 and caution that murine IRG findings may have limited bearing on human IRGM, and the converse caution applies here. The ULK1-binding region of IRGM has not been mapped, so conservation of a binding determinant cannot be checked. I found no study showing mouse Irgm1 binding to any protein kinase.

Own global alignment (Biopython, BLOSUM62) of the packet sequence (Q60766) against A1A4Y4: 101 identical of 180 aligned positions; human IRGM lacks most of the mouse sequence
assertions.limitations: The human ULK1 interaction rests on co-IP and colocalization, and direct binding was not tested. It is possible that mouse Irgm1 binds a kinase, but no such evidence was found.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to human TRIP4/ASC-1 (Q15650, 581 aa). The cryo-EM structure of full-length human ASC1 (TRIP4) bound to ASCC3 (PDB 8ALZ, 3.4 A; Jia, Hilal, Loll & Wahl, Nat Commun 2023) models two zinc ions in the TRIP4 C2HC5-type zinc finger. I checked the struct_conn metal records in the deposited mmCIF. Zn601 is coordinated by Cys171, Cys173, His178 and Cys192 of chain A (TRIP4). Zn602 is coordinated by Cys184, Cys187, Cys200 and Cys203. All eight ligands are present at these positions in the packet sequence. This is direct structural evidence that the protein binds zinc ions, which matches GO:0008270. The InterPro IEA (IPR009349, TRIP4/RQT4 C2HC5 zinc finger) agrees.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 Slr0006 (Q55667, 217 aa). The IBA transfers tRNA binding from E. coli TsaC/YrdC (P45748), which binds tRNA(Thr) (EcoCyc IDA; El Yacoubi et al. 2009; Harris et al. 2011). That inference does not hold for Slr0006. My global alignment gives only 26.7% identity to E. coli TsaC. The TsaC residue Arg52, whose mutation abolishes activity, is not conserved (Phe in Slr0006), and Arg110 is also not conserved. Synechocystis has two other members of the YrdC family: sll1866 (P74144, 41% identical to E. coli TsaC, the likely TsaC ortholog) and sll0216 (P72724, 44% identical to E. coli YciO). Phylogenetic and homology-modelling work defines Slr0006 as the founder of a separate 'Slr0006-like' subfamily found only in cyanobacteria. That subfamily always co-occurs with TsaC and YciO homologs and has a substantially different binding cleft, which the authors take as evidence of a distinct function. The experimental work on Slr0006 itself (CO2-limitation induction, divalent-cation-dependent membrane attachment, co-fractionation with 30S ribosomal proteins and rRNA, and a modelled positively charged cavity) does not show tRNA binding. The function cannot be transferred from TsaC.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to E. coli K-12 GlyS (P00961), the beta subunit of the alpha2beta2 glycyl-tRNA synthetase. The ATP site sits mainly in the catalytic alpha subunit (GlyQ). In the 7EIV crystal structure, every AMP-PNP contact within 4 A is from alpha-subunit residues, according to my parse of the deposited model. Ju et al. 2021 (NAR) nevertheless show that the beta subunit is needed for ATP binding and contributes to it directly. The beta B3 domain folds against alpha to complete the AMP-PNP pocket. Beta Arg326 forms a direct charge interaction with the gamma-phosphate of AMP-PNP; in my parse of 7EIV it lies 4-5 A from AMP-PNP in both beta copies. The R326 mutation reduced glycine activation about 15-fold and decreased aminoacylation. By ITC, ATP bound the holoenzyme with a Kd of about 6 uM, but no binding to the alpha subunit alone was detected. Together these results establish a functional contribution of GlyS to ATP binding by the GlyRS complex. Because the beta subunit does not bind ATP on its own, the evidence supports 'contributes_to' ATP binding rather than 'enables'.

If the curation standard requires the subunit to bind ATP by itself ('enables'), the evidence does not support that. The assertion is accepted only as 'contributes_to'.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to Xenopus laevis atp6ap2.S, the (pro)renin receptor (Q7T0S3). The only support is an InterPro2GO IEA from family IPR012493 (renin receptor-like). A QuickGO query shows that GO:0038023 for the human (O75787), mouse (Q9CYN9), rat (Q6AXS4) and Xenopus orthologs rests on this same InterPro IEA alone, with no experimental annotation in any species. The receptor claim traces to Nguyen et al. 2002, where renin/prorenin binding to overexpressed human (P)RR raised renin catalytic efficiency and activated ERK1/2. The authoritative review I read concludes that this signalling role is not supported in vivo: dissociation constants for renin and prorenin are 1-20 nM whereas plasma concentrations are picomolar (about 0.5 and 5 pmol/L), so direct (pro)renin-dependent activation at circulating levels 'still seems impossible'; the handle-region-peptide blocker failed to block (pro)renin binding or ERK1/2 phosphorylation in vascular smooth muscle cells; and the protein's conserved, essential functions are V-ATPase assembly and acting as a physical adaptor between the Frizzled/LRP6 complex and the V-ATPase in Wnt signalling, which the authors note are '(pro)renin-independent' because (pro)renin is absent in early Xenopus embryos and in Drosophila. That last point bears directly on the supplied protein. An adaptor that couples a receptor complex to a proton pump is not itself receiving and transmitting a signal, and a family-level mapping cannot establish the term for the frog protein when the receptor role is contested in the best-studied species and inapplicable to early frog development.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to rat Hip1r (Q99PW9, 1079 aa, a near-complete entry flagged as a fragment). Clathrin binding is experimentally established for the human/mammalian HIP1R protein. Legendre-Guillemin et al. 2002 showed that HIP12/HIP1R binds directly to clathrin light chain through its central helical (coiled-coil) domain and stimulates clathrin assembly, while lacking the clathrin-box-mediated high-affinity heavy-chain interaction seen for HIP1. Chen & Brodsky 2005 mapped the interaction to the conserved 22-residue sequence of clathrin light chains and showed that light-chain mutations abolishing Hip1R binding also abolish Hip1R-stimulated clathrin assembly. UniProt records HIP1R-CLTB interaction (PubMed:11889126, 15533940) and GO:0030276 IDA for human HIP1R. GO:0030276 explicitly covers binding to a clathrin heavy or light chain, so light-chain binding satisfies the definition. Transfer to rat is well supported: my global alignment gives 91.6% identity to human HIP1R overall and 214/253 identities across the human 347-599 coiled-coil region that carries the light-chain-binding activity.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to mouse AKAP5/AKAP150 (D3YVF0, 745 aa, a reviewed entry). The ISO comes from rat Akap5 (RGD:620829; UniProt P24587), whose GO:0044877 annotations are IPIs from two studies with native multiprotein complexes: Liu et al. 2004 (EMBO J) showed AKAP79/150 is required within a beta2-adrenergic-receptor/BKCa channel signalling complex in which beta2AR simultaneously binds BKCa and Cav1.2, and Gorski et al. 2005 (Mol Biol Cell) isolated intact AKAP79/150-cadherin complexes containing beta-catenin from epithelial cells, cultured neurons and rat brain synaptic membranes, mapping the AKAP binding site in cadherins. Binding a cadherin/beta-catenin assembly or a receptor-channel assembly is binding a macromolecular complex, which matches GO:0044877. The function is also intrinsic to AKAP5 across mammals: it is defined as the high-affinity binding protein for the dimeric PKA RII regulatory subunit and also binds the calcineurin heterodimer, so its characteristic ligands are themselves protein complexes. Mouse-specific interaction work exists too (UniProt cites PubMed:17110924 with experimental evidence on the mouse protein for recruitment of the KCNK2/TREK-1 channel). Rat and mouse AKAP5 are 81.9% identical over the aligned region in my alignment, with the multivalent scaffold architecture (N-terminal basic/targeting regions, PKA-RII-binding helix) shared.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is Mycobacterium tuberculosis CDC1551 MT1671 (Q7D885, 565 aa). By my alignment it is identical to H37Rv Rv1635c (O06152) apart from a 9-residue N-terminal extension from an alternative start. The pentosyltransferase annotation is a TreeGrafter IEA from the GT83/PTHR33908 family, which includes the ArnT L-Ara4N (pentose) transferases. MT1671 itself has been characterized experimentally. Dinadayala et al. 2006 showed that a transposon mutant of MT1671 in M. tuberculosis CDC1551 makes lipoarabinomannan devoid of mannose caps. Expressing MT1671 in M. smegmatis added a single mannose residue to the arabinan termini. MT1671 was therefore identified as the mannosyltransferase that deposits the first cap mannose. Kaur et al. 2008 PNAS refer to Rv1635c as the mannosyltransferase responsible for the first capping Man. The transferred sugar is mannose, a hexose, and UniProt records mannosyltransferase activity (IMP, MTBBASE) for this entry. No evidence shows transfer of a pentosyl group (e.g., arabinose) by this enzyme.

The structure is titled as revealing 'the basis for CREB family selective dimerization and DNA binding', i.e. it is a CREB1 homodimer: one CREB1 molecule bound to an identical CREB1 molecule, which is exactly GO:0042802. The supporting ISO/IEA from human CREB1 is also sound, since human CREB1 has IntAct self-interaction IPIs (PMIDs 20102225, 23661758, 25609649) and mouse and human CREB1 differ at a single residue in my global alignment (326/327 identical).

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to chicken IL34 (R4GIU3, 178 aa). The packet's only provenance is an InterPro IEA (IPR020415), but the inference is well supported on two independent grounds. First, CSF1R binding by IL-34 is directly established in mammals: soluble CSF-1R binds human IL-34 at least as tightly as CSF-1 and biotinylated IL-34 binding to THP-1 cells is blocked by anti-CSF-1R antibody (Lin et al. 2008); mouse IL-34 competes with 125I-CSF-1 on macrophages (Wei et al. 2010); and co-crystal structures define the interface for both species (PDB 4DKD human, 4EXP mouse), with ITC showing the requirement for receptor domains D2-D3. Second, chicken-specific experiments show that the chicken protein acts through chicken CSF1R: recombinant chicken IL-34 elicits macrophage growth from chicken bone marrow cells (Garceau et al. 2010), and in chicken HD11 macrophage and OU2 fibroblast lines, IL-34-induced signalling and proliferation/cytokine responses are blunted by two independent CSF1R siRNAs and by a neutralizing anti-CSF-1R antibody (Truong et al. 2018). Blocking the receptor abolishes the ligand's effects, which is receptor-engagement evidence rather than an unrelated phenotype. The ortholog relationship is solid: chicken IL34 is about 60% identical to human IL34 over the core 145 residues and is under purifying selection. My own mapping of the human IL-34/CSF-1R interface, computed from PDB 4DKD (23 IL-34 residues within 4 A of CSF-1R), onto the chicken sequence shows partial conservation, including D43, K44, L109, E121, L125, L127 and S184, with other positions substituted; such co-evolutionary divergence of a cytokine-receptor pair is expected and does not argue against binding, given that the chicken ligand remains active on chicken cells in a CSF1R-dependent manner.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to human PRR7 (Q8TB68, 274 aa). Although the packet's only provenance is an Ensembl-orthology IEA from rat Prr7, the underlying study provides evidence for the human protein as well. Kravchick et al. 2016 (EMBO J) co-immunoprecipitated endogenous PRR7 from brain lysate together with GluN1, GluN2B and PSD-95 (Fig. 3A), i.e. PRR7 associates with the assembled NMDA-receptor/PSD-95 postsynaptic assembly, where GluN1/GluN2 heteromers are obligate complexes; the association survived stringent RIPA conditions and was reduced by NMDA treatment of neurons (Figs. 3D, 3E). The same paper showed, with human PRR7 plasmids in HEK293 cells, that PRR7 binds GluN1 and mapped the requirement to the transmembrane domain, short N-terminus and first ~15 intracellular residues (Figs. 3B-3D); that region is 60/60 identical between human and rat in my alignment, and the two orthologs are 98.5% identical over aligned positions. The paper additionally places PRR7 in a c-Jun/FBW7-containing complex, with direct in vitro pulldowns for both partners and a stabilised ternary assembly on co-expression (Fig. 5B, 5D, 5F); the human-specific IPIs for JUN and FBXW7 in GO come from this work. Earlier proteomics of the rat forebrain PSD identified PRR7 and showed binding to PSD-95 PDZ3 by IP and GST pulldown, with NR1 and NR2B co-precipitating with PRR7 (Murata et al. 2005). Together these establish binding to macromolecular assemblies as required by GO:0044877.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to Plasmodium falciparum PfAha1 (O97244 = Q689C6, gene PF3D7_0306200 / PFC0270w, 349 aa). Although the packet's provenance is only an InterPro IEA, direct experimental evidence exists for this very protein. Chua et al. 2012 identified PfAha1 and showed, by a directed in vivo split-ubiquitin assay and by in vitro GST pull-down with recombinant proteins, that it interacts with PfHsp90; the interaction required MgCl2 and ATP, was competed by the co-chaperone Pfp23, and was salt-sensitive, and site-directed mutagenesis guided by modelling identified the polar residue N108 as essential for the interaction. PfAha1 also stimulated PfHsp90 ATPase activity, a functional readout of productive binding. I verified that Asn108 is present in the packet sequence (…YAI-N108-IERT…) and that the Aha1/Hch1 family RKGK motif, reported as totally conserved and contacting Hsp90 in the yeast Aha1-N/Hsp82-M co-crystal, is present as R58-K59-G60-K61. GO already carries this result as GO:0051879 'Hsp90 protein binding' IPI (PMID:22100910, with PfHsp90 PF3D7_0708400, assigned by GeneDB). I checked the ontology: GO:0051879 sits under GO:0031072 heat shock protein binding, not under GO:0051087, so the experimental annotation does not propagate; however Hsp90 is a protein-folding chaperone, so binding it satisfies the exact text definition of GO:0051087 ('Binding to a chaperone protein, a class of proteins that bind to nascent or unfolded polypeptides and ensure correct folding or transport').

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to human ZCCHC24 (Q8N2G6, 241 aa; the other accessions are primate orthologs in the same annotation group). The protein contains a retroviral-type CCHC zinc knuckle with all four metal ligands intact at canonical spacing: by regex search of the sequence I found C134-x2-C137-x4-H142-x4-C147 (CHLCFNKGHYIKDC), matching the PROSITE ZF_CCHC pattern that UniProt records at 132-149. This module is defined by its zinc ligands, and its zinc binding is established structurally in homologous proteins: in PDB 3TS2 (mouse LIN28A bound to pre-let-7g, 2.0 A) I parsed the deposited model and found two Zn ions, each coordinated by exactly this arrangement (Cys139/Cys142/His147/Cys152 and Cys161/Cys164/His169/Cys174). An intact, canonical zinc knuckle is a specific metal-binding determinant rather than a generic family resemblance, and ZCCHC24 is independently annotated with RNA binding from high-throughput RNA-interactome capture, consistent with a folded functional knuckle. The protein also carries a second predicted zinc-ribbon module of the ZAR1/RTP1-like 3CxxC type (InterPro IPR033446/IPR027377).

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to human SRRM2/SRm300 (Q9UQ35, 2752 aa). The packet's IBA route is unsound: I verified that its with/from gene MGI:1916205 is mouse Srrm4 (nSR100), a paralog whose own GO:0003729 IDA (PMID:19737518) concerns nSR100 targets, not SRRM2. Direct evidence for the supplied protein exists elsewhere. In the cryo-EM structure of the human post-catalytic P-complex spliceosome (PDB 6QDV, 3.3 A), the SRRM2 chain, which SIFTS maps to residues 1-26 of Q9UQ35 (modelled sequence MYNGIGLPTPRGSGTNGYVQRNLSLV, the N-terminus of the packet sequence), contacts the ligated-exon RNA. I downloaded the mmCIF and computed contacts myself: at a 4.0 A cutoff, 11 SRRM2 residues (Met1, Ile5, Pro10, Arg11, Gly14, Thr15, Asn16, Gly17, Tyr18, Val19, Arg21) lie within range of four nucleotides of chain E, the entity the depositors label 'Ligated exons: MINX mRNA', while no SRRM2 atom is within 4.5 A of the excised intron lariat (chain I). In a post-catalytic spliceosome the exons have been ligated, so this is a direct protein contact with mRNA, matching GO:0003729's definition (UTR and coding sequence, no intron). This is corroborated by zero-length UV-crosslinking evidence in living cells: SRRM2 is recovered as an RNA-binding protein in many poly(A)+ RNA interactome-capture and related datasets (the basis of its GO:0003723 HDA annotations from Castello et al. 2012 and Baltz et al. 2012), and the protein was originally cloned as a factor binding the 5' non-coding sequence of ATBF1 mRNA.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to human ATF4 (P18848, 351 aa). The cited route does not work: the mouse IDA that the ISS and Ensembl IEA are projected from (PMID:23624402, Han et al. 2013) demonstrates ATF4 binding to CHOP/DDIT3 by co-immunoprecipitation, and DDIT3 is a C/EBP-family protein with no CREB name, so that result supports protein heterodimerization activity rather than GO:0008140. A different study does support the term, and GO records it directly on the human protein. Luo et al. 2003 identified 'the closely related ATF1 and CREB1 as nuclear co-factors that form in vivo complexes with endogenous ATF4', and showed by EMSA that in vitro translated ATF4 requires nuclear co-factors to bind the Grp78 ATF/CRE site, forming a complex of the same mobility as the stress-induced complex; ER stress induced CREB1 phosphorylation and ATF1/CREB1 binding at that promoter. ATF1, CREM and CREB1 are the CREB family (InterPro IPR001630), so either partner satisfies the term. On the strength of this work, curators annotated GO:1990589 'ATF4-CREB1 transcription factor complex' as IDA (PMID:12871976) on human ATF4, human CREB1, mouse Atf4 and mouse Creb1, and Complex Portal records the mouse ATF4-CREB1 complex with physical-interaction evidence. Transfer across species is in any case unproblematic: the ATF4 bZIP domain (human 278-341) is 75/77 identical to mouse in my alignment.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to Bluetongue virus 10 VP6-A (Q98829), a minor inner-core protein of this orbivirus, and the only support is an InterPro2GO IEA from IPR001399 (Orbivirus VP6), a family-level mapping that reflects VP6 being a virion protein rather than a demonstrated structural role. The experimentally established activities of this protein are enzymatic and nucleic-acid-binding, not structural: it binds ATP, has RNA-dependent ATPase and dsRNA-unwinding helicase activity (Stauber et al. 1997, PubMed:9311795), its structure-function mutants K110, E157 and R205 were characterized (Kar & Roy 2003, PubMed:14557620), and it forms homohexamers. Current literature places VP6 with the internal replicase/packaging proteins, describing it as an RNA-binding protein that binds plus-sense ssRNA and interacts with VP3 to facilitate RNA encapsidation, while the capsid shell itself is built from VP3 (subcore), VP7 (core surface) and VP2/VP5 (outer capsid). GO:0005198 requires action that contributes to the structural integrity of a complex. Hexamerisation and contact with VP3 during packaging do not establish such a contribution, and recent work reports that genome assortment proceeds independently of VP6. I found no evidence that VP6 contributes to capsid or core structural integrity.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to SIRV1 Hjc (Q98VP9, 121 aa), the Holliday junction resolvase of Sulfolobus islandicus rod-shaped virus 1. Birkenbihl et al. 2001 (J Mol Biol) purified the recombinant SIRV1 and SIRV2 Hjc proteins, each 121 residues and differing by only 18 residues, and showed that 'Both proteins bind selectively to synthetic Holliday-structure analogues with an apparent dissociation constant of 25 nM', with Mg2+-dependent cleavage near the junction. UniProt attributes DNA binding for this entry to that paper with experimental evidence (ECO:0000269|PubMed:11399079), noting that the protein binds four-way junction DNA but not sequence-identical linear duplex DNA. Selective, nanomolar binding to a defined DNA structure by the purified protein directly satisfies GO:0003677, and the specificity for a junction excludes nonspecific association as an explanation.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to mouse Ppp1r15a/GADD34 (MyD116; P17564, 657 aa). Human GADD34 binding to PP1 is firmly established: Connor et al. 2001 (Mol Cell Biol) mapped PP1 binding to GADD34 residues 483-619 and isolated cellular GADD34/PP1 complexes, with the GADD34-bound PP1 active as an eIF2alpha phosphatase; UniProt also records several IPIs with the PP1 catalytic subunit PPP1CA (P62136), and there is a co-crystal structure of PP1-alpha with the GADD34 PP1-binding domain (PDB 4XPN, 2.3 A), whose GADD34 chain (UniProt O75807) begins KARKVRFSEKVTVHFLAVWAGPAQAARQGPWEQLARDRSR, i.e. the canonical RVxF docking motif plus the adjacent region. Transfer to mouse is well supported at the level of the actual binding determinant: in my alignment of human 553-621 onto the mouse protein the region is 58/69 identical, and the RVxF motif is present as KVHF (K-V-H-F) at mouse residues 548-551, which fits the [RK]-[VIL]-x-[FW] consensus, with the flanking W-containing segment that contacts PP1 in 4XPN and 7NXV essentially conserved. Overall mouse/human identity is only about 55%, but the divergence lies outside this PP1-binding module.

The mouse motif is KVHF rather than the human KVRF; the substituted position is the degenerate 'x' of the consensus, but I did not find a direct measurement of mouse GADD34 affinity for PP1.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to human FAM3D (Q96BQ1, 224 aa; the packet's two fragment accessions are the human and chimpanzee entries carrying the same rule-based annotation). The only support is UniProt rule UR001922981 (ProRule PRU01375, 'GG-type lectin domain', condition PROSITE PS52031), which asserts the Lectin keyword and GO:0030246 for the whole family. No FAM3 protein has been tested for carbohydrate binding. The lectin label derives from a distant structural relative: the POMGNT1 stem domain, which binds beta-GlcNAc and GalNAcbeta1-3GlcNAc in co-crystals and shares the FAM3B fold at about 20% identity and 1.7 A Ca RMSD. Crystal structures of FAM3B/PANDER (2YOP/2YOQ) and FAM3C/ILEI (5LC2-5LC4) show a globular beta-beta-alpha fold with a conserved water-filled cavity and no bound sugar, and the FAM3B paper proposes no ligand. FAM3D's own characterized molecular activity is as a high-affinity agonist of the formyl peptide receptors FPR1 and FPR2; no glycan array, lectin assay, GAG-binding or sugar co-crystal data exist for it. The only direct sugar-binding test on another GG-domain protein, human TMEM2 versus hyaluronan by SEC and glycan microarray, was negative. I did verify, by computing contacts in PDB 5GGP and aligning, that the POMGNT1 sugar-contacting residues are largely conserved in FAM3D (R129, Y152, D179, R207 align to R99, Y122, D148, R176, with E180 to D149 and W234 to Y206), so the inference is plausible, but a conserved surface without any binding measurement on this family does not establish the activity.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to mouse Cemip2/TMEM2 (Q5FWI3, 1383 aa). The ISS/ISO/IEA chain derives from a single human IDA citing Yamamoto et al. 2017, and that paper tested only mouse TMEM2, so the evidence actually concerns the packet protein. What it shows is a cofactor requirement, not binding: membrane fractions from cells expressing mouse TMEM2-FLAG depolymerized fluorescent hyaluronan in HEPES pH 7.0 with 1 mM CaCl2 but not without it (Fig. 2C). There was no chelation control, no Ca2+ titration beyond 0 versus 1 mM, no test of other divalent cations, and no binding measurement. The paper's candidate Ca2+ site, a pectate-lyase-like DQD motif, was not supported by its own mutagenesis: D275N, E260N/D262Q and E281Q/E283Q retained wild-type activity. The one experimental structure (human TMEM2 ectodomain, PDB 8C6I, 3.5 A) models no Ca2+; its authors note that of the two acidic residues that coordinate the catalytic Ca2+ in the homologous chondroitin B lyase only one is conserved and that there are no other suitable Ca2+ ligands nearby. Neither UniProt entry records a Ca2+ BINDING or METAL site; the mouse entry lists only a COFACTOR Ca(2+) line from the same 2017 paper. A requirement of Ca2+ in the assay buffer, with no site identified and candidate-site mutants active, does not establish that the protein binds a calcium ion as GO:0005509 requires.

assertions.rationale: The packet sequence is identical to Saccharomyces cerevisiae Elf1 (P36053, 145 aa). The packet's only provenance is an RCA annotation citing a bioinformatic/proteomic survey of the yeast zinc proteome, which by itself is computational. However, direct structural evidence now exists for this exact protein. In PDB 8RAM (2.8 A cryo-EM structure of a Sen1-bound Pol II pre-termination complex; Nat Struct Mol Biol 2025), chain M is the 'Transcription elongation factor 1' entity covering Elf1 residues 1-145, and my parse of the deposited mmCIF found a zinc ion bound to that chain coordinated by Cys25, Cys28, Cys49 and Cys52 at 2.2-2.4 A. These are precisely the four positions UniProt lists as Zn(2+) BINDING sites (inferred there by similarity to human ELOF1), and they lie in the protein's Zn-ribbon domain (Pfam PF05129 Zn_ribbon_Elf1). A modelled, fully coordinated Zn site in a 2.8 A structure of the native yeast protein establishes zinc ion binding.

summary: All 25 supplied assertions (25 proteins, one assertion each) were reviewed; none left unreviewed. Decisions: 16 accept, 9 do not accept, 0 needs adjudication. Support types: 9 experimental, 7 inference, 9 none established. Relations recorded: 15 enables, 1 contributes_to, 9 null. Accepted cases rested either on direct evidence for the supplied sequence (structural zinc sites in TRIP4 and yeast Elf1, Holliday-junction DNA binding by SIRV1 Hjc, the mouse CREB1 bZIP homodimer crystal structure, SRRM2 contacting ligated-exon mRNA in the human P-complex spliceosome, PfAha1-PfHsp90 pulldowns, PRR7 in NMDAR/PSD-95 and c-Jun/FBW7 assemblies, ATF4 complexes with ATF1/CREB1) or on orthology inferences where the functional determinants were checked and conserved (rat TRPML1 Fe2+ channel, rat CD44 signalling, rat HIP1R clathrin-light-chain binding, mouse AKAP5 complex binding, mouse GADD34 RVxF motif for PP1, chicken IL34 acting through CSF1R, human ZCCHC24 zinc knuckle, and E. coli GlyS contributing to ATP binding within the GlyRS heterotetramer). Rejections fell into three groups: family- or rule-level propagation contradicted by the enzyme's characterized specificity (RgtB and MT1671 annotated pentosyltransferase although they transfer galacturonic acid and mannose respectively; FAM3D's rule-based lectin label), terms whose exact definition the evidence does not reach (NDE1 microtubule binding, where purified NudE does not co-sediment with microtubules; BTV VP6 structural molecule activity for a helicase/RNA-packaging protein; TMEM2 calcium ion binding resting on one +/- CaCl2 activity test with no identified site), and transfers across proteins too divergent or too contested to carry the function (Synechocystis Slr0006 from E. coli TsaC; mouse Irgm1 from the truncated human IRGM; Xenopus atp6ap2 signalling receptor activity, which the (pro)renin-receptor literature disputes). Several accepted entries note relation nuances: GlyS supports contributes_to rather than enables, and SRRM2's mRNA contact is complex-dependent. Evidence published after the GOA 2026-07-29 snapshot is flagged where used (notably PDB 8RAM for Elf1 zinc binding).
